chunks: And it is reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The morning of the day of the Night of Power is like the Night of Power, so act and strive [in worship].

key_terms.اعمل واجتهد: Act and strive — an imperative urging the believer to perform acts of worship, supplication, and devotion with full effort
key_terms.صبيحة: The morning, the dawn of a day — specifically the morning immediately following Laylat al-Qadr
key_terms.ليلة القدر: Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power or Decree — one of the last odd nights of Ramadan, described in Quran (97) as better than a thousand months

ai.seo_question: Is the morning after Laylat al-Qadr also blessed according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the blessing and spiritual significance of Laylat al-Qadr (Night of Power) extends into the morning that follows it. The morning of that day carries the same immense spiritual reward as the night itself. This teaching was addressed to the Shia community as an encouragement to continue worship and devotion throughout the full span of this blessed occasion, not limiting their efforts to the night hours alone.
